title: The caliph finds him
hookLine: Caliph Umar, sent by a dream, brings him gold, and the harper weeps at being seen (Masnavi 1)

cards: Being noticed when nobody seemed to be looking can be a strange thing. The teacher who stopped you in the hall to say she'd read what you wrote. The boss who remembered the thing you did quietly months ago.

A stranger who saw you were struggling and just asked. Someone can hold it together for years, and one person really seeing them is what brings the tears. The old harper is asleep on a grave, his harp for a pillow.

teach.h: A DREAM, AND SEVEN HUNDRED DINARS.
teach.b: While the harper sleeps, the caliph Umar also falls asleep, and a voice comes to him in a dream. A servant of God is lying in the graveyard, it says: take seven hundred gold dinars from the treasury and bring them to him.
Umar goes. He walks the whole graveyard and sees nobody but an old man asleep.
Surely not him. He circles again. Still only the old man.
Then it dawns on him: this is the one. So the caliph himself stands over a worn-out musician, the kind of man people pass without a glance, and waits by him until he stirs.
The harper opens his eyes, sees the caliph, and starts to shake. He assumes he's in trouble. Umar tells him not to be afraid; he has come with good news.
God sends greetings, and this gold, and there's more when it runs out. That's when the harper breaks.
He weeps, and in Rumi's telling he flings his harp down and smashes it, crying out that it had stood between him and God. He mourns all the years he spent performing. The gold barely matters.
What undoes him is that he was seen. Sufi readers take the heart of the story to be this: the one nobody wanted, playing to empty graves, had an audience after all.

how: In Sufi teaching, stories like this one are read as a picture of God noticing the forgotten, and many readers take it as a reason to look for the people others pass by.

o: a leader of the Muslim community, a caliph
a Muslim scholar who teaches the law
a holy man who lives alone in the desert

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.

s: Umar recognized the harper right away
he circled the graveyard, saw only an old man, and thought, surely not him.
when he woke, the harper was afraid
seeing the caliph, he shook, thinking he was in trouble.
the harper weeps mostly because of the gold
in the story, what undoes him is being seen by God. the gold barely matters.

games.q: you're Umar. a dream sent you to find God's servant in the graveyard, and all you can find is an old harper asleep on a grave. what do you do?
o: decide the dream was wrong and go home.
keep searching for someone more respectable.
realize he is the one, and wait beside him.
games.why: after circling twice, Umar understands the old musician is the one, and waits for him to wake.

practice: Let someone come to mind who gets passed by: the person who cleans the building, the quiet cousin, the neighbor who lives alone, an older relative who doesn't get many calls.
Hold them in mind with no plan, and just see them, the way Umar finally saw the old man on the grave. If you pray, you can hold them there too.

wordCard.voice: Khalifa. The Arabic word for caliph, the leader of the Muslim community; Umar, who found the old harper, was the second. Today's word.

orig.note: Persian, from Arabic khalifa: the caliph, the leader of the Muslim community. Umar was the second.

carryVoice: Your line: you were seen. Seven hundred dinars mattered less than that. That's day one hundred ninety.
